title: Examen de nivel A2
description: Demuestra que tienes el nivel A2 del Marco Común Europeo (MCER): gramática, vocabulario, comprensión lectora y comprensión auditiva.

syllabus.label: Present simple y present continuous; verbos de estado
Phrasal verbs comunes (get up, look for, turn off…)
Contables e incontables: how much / many, a lot of, too, enough, all / both / none / most
Past simple: negativas, preguntas e irregulares
Past continuous y past simple (when / while)
Contar una historia: first, then, finally y adverbios de modo
Comparativos, (not) as … as, the same as, similar to, different from
Planes: be going to, present continuous y Shall we…?
Present perfect: experiencias, just / already / yet
would like y verbo + to (want, decide, need)
Repaso de A1 que el Core Inventory pide en A2: 's / s', mine / yours, in / on / at, can / could, imperativos, adverbios de frecuencia, like + -ing, very / quite
Vocabulario: la casa y la rutina
Vocabulario: tiempo libre, recuerdos y celebraciones

variants.title: A weekend in Edinburgh
variants.text:
Last weekend I visited Edinburgh with my friend Kate. First, we took the train from London. The journey was long, but it wasn't boring because we played cards and talked all the time.

On Saturday morning we walked up to the castle. It's the most famous place in the city, and the views are amazing. Then we had lunch in a small café near the castle. The soup was the best soup I have ever eaten!

In the afternoon it started to rain, so we went to a museum. Kate was very interested in the old clothes, but I was a bit tired.

Now I'm writing this on the train home. Kate is sleeping next to me. It's raining again, of course. Edinburgh is colder and wetter than London, but I want to go back soon!

Tom

variants.title: My first month in Cork
variants.text:
Hi everyone! I moved to Cork, in Ireland, a month ago. I work as a waitress in a busy café near the river, and this month I'm also helping in the kitchen.

The first week was very tiring. First, I got lost every day! Then I lost my phone on the bus. Finally, a nice man found it and brought it to the café.

Cork is smaller than Dublin, but I think it's the friendliest city in Ireland. People always say hello and talk to you in the street.

Last Sunday I went to the English Market. It's the oldest food market in the city, and I bought cheese, bread and some amazing chocolate. The weather was terrible, with wind and rain all day, but I was too excited to care.

Ana
